body.name: Explicit legal collision path \(\mathfrak C_N\)
body.construction: Fix \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \(g=0\), \(r=1\), and the binary alphabet ordered as \(0<1\).  Fix the chart \(\mathcal U=(\epsilon,0,1)\) and \(\mathcal V=((\epsilon,R),(\epsilon,A),(0,A))\).  Under the baseline-symbol convention in \(\mathcal D_{K-1}\), fix \(\mathcal D_2=(I_3,\bar B_1,\bar B_1^2)\), \(\mathcal F=(I_3,\bar B_1)\), and \(d=2\).  For all sufficiently large \(N\), evaluate the explicitly declared \(\eta_N=N^{-1/4}\), \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\), base parameters \(\alpha_{\star},P_{\star},S_{\star}\), hazards \(h_N^{(0)},h_N^{(1)}\), emissions \(B_{0,N}^{\star},B_{1,N}^{\star}\), and transformed transition \(P_N^{(1)}\).  These parameters induce the two six-date stopped-panel laws \(P_{W,N}^{(0)}\) and \(P_{W,N}^{(1)}\) with the same deterministic treated-outcome law.  Set \(\mathfrak C_N=(P_{W,N}^{(0)},P_{W,N}^{(1)})\), and evaluate its target only at \(\mu^0_{0,1}\) and \(\tau_{0,1}\).
